Calculating eccentricity

e = d(P, F) / d(P, L) = cos β / cos α

F is the focus, L the directrix, α the cone’s half-angle, and β the angle between the cutting plane and cone axis.

Conic section guide

Circle e = 0
A perpendicular cut through one nappe. Every point is the same distance from the center.
Ellipse 0 < e < 1
A tilted, closed cut through one nappe. The sum of distances to its two foci is constant.
Parabola e = 1
A cut parallel to a cone generator. Each point is equally distant from the focus and directrix.
Hyperbola e > 1
A cut through both nappes. The absolute difference of distances to its two foci is constant.
Plane equation

z − 2 = 0
